text:
sophie: FYI customer reports intermittent 429s during nightly batch, says project quota looks fine on the dashboard, but they're seeing bursts fail behind a NATed CPE.
sophie: pasted their minimal repro:
```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-ABC" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"ping"}' &
done
```
sophie: response snippet from their logs (they truncated):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1672531200
X-RateLimit-Scope: ip
x-request-id: 01H7K2ZQ9
```
sophie: customer says the header shows scope=ip even though the request included their API key header.
raj: interesting — that header indicates the limiter credited the NATed source IP not the API key. could be a race in authz ordering.
raj: quick check: are we running the new multi-scope precedence change on the prod edge for their region? if not, requests might be short-circuiting to IP scope.
olivia: I can confirm last deploy toggled the precedence flag for eu-west but not us-east. what's the customer's region?
sophie: they're in us-east-1.
olivia: ok that's the issue then — we forgot to flip the precedence for the NAT detection rollout in us-east. by default current behavior: if IP scope check completes before API key resolution (proxy cache miss) limiter attributes to IP.
leah: does this match the billing mismatch ticket? they mentioned org_quota not decreasing when using api key from another org.
raj: separate but related: we have two orthogonal problems: (1) attribution precedence (IP vs key), (2) mis-bound API keys (same raw key accidentally provisioned in two projects/orgs). both can surface as surprising 429s.
raj: repro steps I'd like to run from our side to simulate their environment:
1) run 2x workers from a single NATed VM, each sending bursts with same API key.
2) toggle precedence flag off/on and compare which scope wins in the logs.
3) capture authz trace: `grep 01H7K2ZQ9 /var/log/edge/authz/*.log`

raj: expected: with precedence=key we should see `attribution:key` in limiter trace, and header X-RateLimit-Scope:key. with precedence=ip we see `attribution:ip`.
sophie: customer also saw a mismatch with quota page — they say project Q=100k, org Q=1M, but bursts hit project limit and then org didn't step in.
olivia: that's expected if the token is resolved to an API key tied to a different project than the request's downstream routing. e.g., cross-org API key reuse + org-level fallback was disabled for that customer.
leah: customer on an enterprise plan — probably had org-level reserved capacity but fallback path has a bug: when API key provenance differs from source IP org mapping, fallback doesn't kick.
raj: I can reproduce locally. starting a NATed container now.
ratebot: deploy-check: edge-config(us-east) precedenceFlag=false
raj: confirmed reproduction: when precedenceFlag=false the limiter attributes to ip and uses the IP bucket. IP bucket runs out -> 429. even though API key bucket still had tokens.
raj: logs:
```
edge-limiter: request_id=01H7K2ZQ9 src_ip=34.201.12.3 auth_status=pending api_key=sk-prod-ABC
auth-service: resolved api_key -> org_id=org-999 project_id=proj-abc
edge-limiter: attribution=ip bucket=ip:34.201.12.3 remaining=0
```
raj: suggested fix: flip precedenceFlag to true for us-east and patch limiter to wait for auth resolution up to 50ms before attributing to IP bucket; fallback to IP only if auth latency > threshold.
olivia: i can flip the flag in us-east canary now and monitor metrics. need SRE signoff for the short wait change.
leah: from account side i'll prepare a customer note: "we've identified NAT-attribution as root cause; short-term we will toggle precedence to prefer API key; medium-term we'll ship small rate-limiter change to reduce attribution races."
sophie: customer asked for a workaround now — can we ask them to rotate the key and bind the new key to their project explicitly? would that avoid IP attribution? or their proxy still NATs so will still see IP scope unless precedence flips.
raj: rotation won't help if precedence remains false; but it helps detect mis-bound keys. recommend rotate + temporarily decrease burst on client side.
olivia: doing canary toggle now -> will post back.
ratebot: rollout(us-east-precedenceFlag) started -> roll id rf-2026-03-17-01
olivia: toggled on in canary (5% traffic) — canary metrics show X-RateLimit-Scope shifting to key for 98% of the canary traces.
raj: good sign. let's expand to 50% if no regressions for 15m.
leah: I'll escalate to solutions/sales for a credit review if customer has production impact overnight.
sophie: customer updated: after our quick fix they saw errors drop immediately. thanks team :thumbsup:
olivia: rolling to 50% now.
raj: follow-up action items:
- olivia: expand rollout to 50% then full us-east if stable (ops runbook updated) [ETA 1h]
- raj: propose PR to limiter to wait up to 50ms for auth resolution before attributing to IP [ETA 3d]
- leah: prepare customer communication & credit calc [ETA 2h]
- sophie: confirm with customer once fully rolled to us-east and close ticket [ETA 4h]
sophie: copying thread into the ticket. closing here for now. will reopen if they regress.
